caseName: An upper stage electrical system: the heater that dominates the energy, the wire that voltage drop sizes, and the valve drive that gives three quarters of it back
linkedCaseNote: The heater load and the valve count come from the fluidSystems hydrazine monopropellant case. Restated here so the example runs standalone; the coupling is that a fluid system full of solenoid valves, heaters and transducers is an electrical system.

bus.voltageNote: 28 V is the launch vehicle default. The example also sweeps it, because bus voltage is the one architecture decision that moves harness mass quadratically.

phases.name: pad hold
phases.note: Two hours on internal power before launch, cold soaked.

phases.name: coast
phases.note: One hour coast before the circularisation burn.

loads.name: propellant line heaters
loads.note: Keeping hydrazine above its 2 C freezing point. The duty cycle is a thermal assumption rather than an electrical one, and it is the least examined number in the budget.

loads.name: valve drive
loads.note: Four solenoid valves driven continuously. The example shows what peak and hold does to this line.

loads.name: thrust vector actuators
loads.note: The peak driver, and not the energy driver.

loads.name: pyro bus
loads.note: Two NSI initiators fired in parallel. Large power for milliseconds, so it sizes nothing.

battery.temperatureNote: Cold soaked on the pad. This is the case that decides the capacity, not the flight temperature.

harness._comment: A representative run from the power distribution unit to a load at the far end of the stage. The bundle size and altitude are what turn a free-air ampacity into a real one.

runs.note: Main bus feed, out and return.

solenoid._comment: One of the four propellant valves. The coil resistance is quoted at 20 C and the hot case is what the design has to work at.
